A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. All substantive material can be matched; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original bias-mitigation experiments on MNIST, CheXpert, CelebA, and Civil Comments, including subgroup, noise, and dataset-size analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the supplementary comparisons and ablations in the appendices.

M1.justification: The mitigation procedures, architectures, objectives, and subgroup constructions are unchanged. The corrected method-family reference in Section 3.1.3 agrees with the existing Appendix A.2 explanation and does not indicate an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets and classification tasks, including the same subgroup-noise, granularity, and weaker-spurious-correlation scenarios.

E2.justification: The ERM, gDRO, resampling, DomainInd, and CFair comparisons are retained. Appendix C also preserves the same JTT comparisons, with no changes in comparator membership.

E3.justification: Experimental settings, sample sizes, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Table 1 removes the P(S = 1) = 0.5 row, but the unchanged full probability vectors in Section 3.2 and Appendix E still specify that marginal.

E4.justification: The same granularity, annotation-noise, random-grouping, KL-correlation, weaker-correlation, and dataset-size analyses appear in both versions. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across three random seeds, together with the same correlation coefficients and associated p-values. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 changes the reported AUC improvement from more than 0.10 to more than 0.07, and degradation from up to 0.04 to up to 0.08. Figure 2 also reclassifies the 50%-noisy (A, Y) grouping through its annotations. The underlying plotted bars and numerical result tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The distribution definitions, generalisation bounds, KL-minimisation formulation, and Appendix E calculations are unchanged. Correcting the spelling of Kullback-Leibler adds no mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about subgroup choice, potentially harmful mitigation, distribution recovery, and using different subgroups for mitigation and fairness evaluation.

C2.justification: Section 3.1.3 changes 'latter' to 'former', correctly attributing the need for mixed-class subgroups to model-based methods rather than reweighting methods. This resolves a local explanatory inconsistency with the unchanged Appendix A.2. The broader mechanism discussion and limitations remain intact.

D1.justification: The dataset-construction instructions, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and compute disclosures, and code-link target are unchanged in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are retained. No substantive citation or research-positioning change was found.

P1.justification: There are localized grammar, punctuation, and spelling corrections, including the abstract and Kullback-Leibler terminology. Section 5.2 slightly revises its generality wording. The section organization and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adjusts its red brackets and labels, placing the 50%-noisy (A, Y) grouping within the improvement annotation. Table 1 loses one redundant marginal-probability row, with minor surrounding reflow. Other figures, tables, and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reporting accuracy and internal consistency: Section 3.1.3 now agrees with Appendix A.2, and Section 5.2's revised numerical summary better matches Figure 2. These are useful local corrections; the empirical evidence, theoretical analysis, and limitations are otherwise unchanged.
